# Expected values: BigQuery answers recorded from unverified/round.txt.

SELECT ROUND(x, 3000000000) FROM UNNEST([1.5]) x
=> "1.5"

SELECT ROUND(x, -3000000000) FROM UNNEST([1.5]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 9223372036854775807) FROM UNNEST([3.1415925]) x
=> "3.1415925"

SELECT ROUND(x, -9223372036854775808) FROM UNNEST([3.1415925]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 40000) FROM UNNEST([1.0]) x
=> "1.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, -40000) FROM UNNEST([1.0]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, -309) FROM UNNEST([1.6e308]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 308) FROM UNNEST([1.6e308]) x
=> "1.6E308"

SELECT ROUND(x, 324) FROM UNNEST([4.94065645841247e-324]) x
=> "4.9E-324"

SELECT ROUND(x, 323) FROM UNNEST([4.94065645841247e-324]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 3) FROM UNNEST([1.2345]) x
=> "1.234"

SELECT ROUND(x, 6) FROM UNNEST([75.736617999999993]) x
=> "75.736618"

SELECT ROUND(x, 5) FROM UNNEST([0.01207]) x
=> "0.01207"

SELECT ROUND(x, 2) FROM UNNEST([CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)]) x
=> "Infinity"

SELECT ROUND(x, -2) FROM UNNEST([CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)]) x
=> "NaN"

# BigQuery returns positive zero at GoogleSQL's early zero exit, as TRUNC does, and keeps the
# sign with zero digits and where a value rounds to zero past that exit, below 2^-6 at one digit.

SELECT ROUND(x, 0) FROM UNNEST([-0.1]) x
=> "-0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, -1) FROM UNNEST([-1.0]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, -400) FROM UNNEST([-1.0]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 1) FROM UNNEST([-0.01]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 2) FROM UNNEST([-1e-100]) x
=> "0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 1) FROM UNNEST([-0.03]) x
=> "-0.0"

SELECT ROUND(x, 1) FROM UNNEST([-0.04]) x
=> "-0.0"
